raw_response:
My thinking, as I would say it:

I am old now, 75 years, and my hands know this land better than my eyes. I have 14 mu. I do like my neighbors do, and I do like my father did before me. Each year I write nothing — I remember in my head.

I split the land. About 9 mu I keep for wheat in winter, then maize right after in summer — same ground, two crops, this is how we do here in Quzhou. The other 5 mu I keep for cotton, because my wife and I have always grown some cotton and I know this work. Cotton is more trouble, many sprays, but the price is sometimes good.

For wheat, I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer under the plough when I sow in October — that is about 80 jin per mu, so 40 kg. Then after winter, when the wheat wakes up green in spring, I spread 1 bag of urea — 40 jin per mu, about 20 kg. I water 3 times — once before winter so the roots do not freeze dry, once at green-up, once when the head is filling. I spray maybe 2 times for the yellow rust and the aphids. My neighbor Old Wang got 900 jin per mu last year; I hope for 800 jin, that is 400 kg.

For maize after wheat, I do not plough — I just clean the stubble a little and plant with the seeder. I use hybrid seed from the shop at the town, the one my son-in-law told me about, Zhengdan or whatever number is fresh. I put 1 bag compound when planting and 1 bag urea at the knee-high stage. Water 2 times if the sky does not give rain. Spray once for borer. Expect maybe 1000 jin per mu, 500 kg.

For cotton, I plough in spring. I use improved seed, not hybrid — hybrid cotton seed is too expensive for me. I put more fertilizer because cotton eats heavy — 2 bags compound as base, then 1 bag urea at squaring, and a half bag more at flowering. Cotton needs many sprays, at least 6 times for bollworm and aphid and mirid bug, this is the tiring part. Water 3 times. I hope 400 jin seed cotton per mu, 200 kg.

I do not change much from last year. Change is risk. A bad harvest is a disaster; some extra fertilizer is only money.
